Yoga helped her through hardship; she teaches it to bring peace and joy to her community. She shared a photo of two women in wheelchairs hugging, described as their last photo together.

A family album showed her parents’ 1993 wedding; she called them a beautiful couple. Deborah and her husband are close and happy through love, openness, and mutual support.
- 26 Jan 2023: Deborah’s yoga group gave her a handwritten note praising her positive influence. She practices at various places, including her late mother’s home. Her mother read by the window every night with a smile; reading and travel were passions. Photos showed the window seat and an airplane sky view.
- Jolene keeps snakes because they calm and make her happy. Snakes include Susie (shown emerging from a bed) and Seraphim (peeking from a blanket). Seraphim once escaped during a video game and coiled beside her. Jolene said she bought “it” a year earlier in Paris; the referent is unclear.
- Jolene and her boyfriend/partner enjoy gaming. They played *Detroit*; one photo showed someone in bed with a dog watching TV. Jolene has played games since childhood and learned independently. They planned to play *The Walking Dead* on 28 Jan 2023.
- 31 Jan–1 Feb 2023: Deborah met neighbor Anna at yoga in the park. Jolene worked on a difficult but enjoyable robotics project assigned by her professor, designing/programming a robot like solving a puzzle. She was nervous, then proud when it worked. She and her partner chose gaming together instead of resuming yoga.
- 3–4 Feb 2023: Deborah and Anna practiced Warrior II and a seated chair twist (sit at edge, feet planted, twist with hand on knee, breathe, switch sides), stretching back/shoulders and releasing tension. A dance-studio pose photo was shared.
- Jolene’s major engineering project was a sustainable water purifier for a rural community. Planning, research, design, and construction culminated in seeing it provide clean water, which felt surreal, satisfying, and purposeful. She wants sustainable engineering solutions for disadvantaged communities.
- Jolene shared a bookshelf. She likes *Sapiens* and read Neal Stephenson’s *Avalanche* in one sitting around 21 Jan 2023; its story reinforced her belief that effort and belief can overcome obstacles.
- Deborah received flowers from a struggling friend symbolizing hope, courage, warmth, and appreciation. Peaceful places include a forest-trail park, nearby beach, and waterside spot near her mother’s old home. She shared flower, island-with-lone-boat, and woman-with-gold-chain/mother’s-amulet photos. Holding the amulet brings comfort, closeness, love, and strength. Anna also wears a mother-commemorating pendant.
- Jolene shared a summer 2022 Bogotá beach-at-sunset photo with a surfboard. Nature calms her; she wants to try beach yoga. Deborah praised the waves/fresh air and asked for a report.
- 8–9 Feb 2023: Jolene completed a mini-retreat, gaining confidence, a new outlook, and willingness to leave her comfort zone. She was exploring green technology for disadvantaged communities and proposed engineers/volunteers teach STEM to underprivileged children through schools/community centers, workshops, and career speakers. She had not yet contacted organizations. She shared planner sketches; Deborah supported her.
- 21–22 Feb 2023: Jolene had dinner/drinks with friends on 21 February. Deborah visited a nostalgic flower garden; roses and dahlias brought peace. Her friend Karlie died the week before. Deborah shared their last photo, taken in summer 2022 on a hike while riding a motorcycle on a dirt road; it makes her smile. Deborah’s favorite trip was Bali in 2022, peaceful and ideal for yoga; she shared a beach-swing photo.
- 25 Feb 2023: Jolene struggled to balance engineering school and gaming with her partner but made time for yoga/meditation, which provide perspective, alertness, and motivation. Her partner sometimes joins; a photo showed them holding hands with rings. They are unmarried, have been together three years, and are taking it slowly; his ring is decorative. They met in an engineering-college class, became friends, then partners, and collaborate on engineering projects.
- When overwhelmed, Jolene takes breaks, breathes, or meditates. Deborah’s routine includes morning meditation, yoga, teaching, and evenings with loved ones. On 24 Feb 2023 Deborah jogged for the first time in a nearby park and planned to jog daily; exercise helps her feel connected to her body. She shared a sunset/bench photo and said, “Can’t pour from an empty cup.”
- 2 Mar 2023: Anna brought Deborah vegan tofu-and-vegetable stir-fry with ginger and soy sauce. Jolene’s favorite dish is lasagna. Jolene was busy with studies, exams, deadlines, and an endless to-do list, but yoga/meditation helped her relax. Photos showed a wooden-floored room with a window and a purse beside a plant.
- Around 26 Feb 2023, Jolene took Seraphim to a park; it enjoyed the outing. A photo appeared lizard-like despite her calling Seraphim a tamed snake. They explore new places and surprise people. Nature, birdsong, and a gentle breeze help both women slow down.
- Deborah advised Jolene to break work into smaller tasks, set goals, and use a planner while preserving personal time; she offered a mug like a pictured yellow cup with an encouraging handwritten message, which cheered Jolene.
- 13 Mar 2023: Deborah reconnected after a gap and said she had started a neighborhood yoga class. She hosted the first class on Friday; a group photo showed women. Teaching calms her, spreads peace/awareness, creates happiness, and builds community.
- Jolene said engineering assignments were hard to manage and she was struggling to keep up. They agreed to discuss time management when schedules allowed; she would check and respond. Both exchanged warm encouragement.

22 Mar 2023 (Session 10):
- Jolene described deadlines and projects as stressful “catch-up.” She uses the Pomodoro Technique (25 minutes work/5-minute break) but struggles to prioritize.
- Deborah shared photos of her daily to-do list and explained the Eisenhower Matrix: sort tasks into four categories by urgency and importance. Jolene found the visualization helpful and agreed to try it.
- Deborah reminded her to rest and care for herself, then shared a beach/surfboard photo, saying she and Anna had watched a sunset and realized they inspire each other. Jolene said it made her think about learning to surf. She has gathered information, watched videos, bought a beginner’s guide, and needs to find time/place for a lesson. Deborah encouraged her to take step-by-step action, believe in herself, and enjoy the experience; Jolene felt motivated and thanked her.
